title: Peer Guide
description:
About North-Star Care

NorthStar Care (NSC) is a startup founded in 2020 focused on providing comprehensive, next generation, virtual treatment to patients suffering from Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD). The company uses cutting edge genetic and diagnostic testing to create personalized treatment plan for every patient. All patient appointments are performed via telehealth and care coordination is orchestrated seamlessly using North-Star Care’s mobile app. Peer support sessions are performed from the comfort of the patient’s home using virtual reality for a 100% anonymous experience.

NSC is a US-based, 100% remote company that welcomes and encourages diversity of all kinds. NSC is committed to recruiting; training and supporting staff who identify as Black, Indigenous and People of Color; bicultural/bilingual Spanish. As a company, we are committed to undoing systems of oppression and the harms they have caused. We actively work toward building an anti-racist environment and a sense of belonging.

To learn more about North-Star, visit https://www.northstarcare.com.

Job Overview

The Peer Guide serves as a compassionate, patient-centered support specialist within NorthStar’s multidisciplinary Care Team. Drawing on personal lived experience with Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) and Substance Use Disorder (SUD), the Peer Guide walks alongside patients as they navigate their own path of healing and transformation. This role embodies NorthStar’s core belief that healing happens in relationship, and that every individual is the expert of their own recovery journey.

The Peer Guide provides both individual and group support through NorthStar’s virtual engagement platforms, including telehealth and virtual reality (VR), ensuring a trauma-informed, harm reduction-oriented presence throughout every interaction.

Organizational Context

NorthStar is a 100% remote behavioral health organization founded in 2020, providing next-generation virtual treatment to adults with Alcohol Use Disorder and Substance Use Disorder and co-occurring conditions. NSC integrates pharmacogenomic testing, remote biometric monitoring, virtual reality therapy, and AI-assisted care coordination to deliver personalized, evidence-informed treatment at scale.

NorthStar is deeply committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and actively recruits, supports, and develops staff who identify as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color, and/or who are bicultural or bilingual in Spanish. We are an anti-racist organization dedicated to dismantling systems of oppression in behavioral health care.

Essential Responsibilities

The following responsibilities reflect the core functions of the Peer Guide role. Additional duties may be assigned consistent with organizational needs for peer support services.

Direct Peer Support Services

  • Engage patients in a strengths-based, trauma-informed manner, affirming each person as the expert of their own healing and recovery goals.
  • Provide individual peer support via telephone, video conferencing, and Virtual Reality (VR) platforms, connecting with patients at least weekly during initial treatment phases.
  • Facilitate and co-facilitate virtual peer support groups and recovery-focused educational sessions, including VR-based group programming.
  • Share personal lived experience with AUD and SUD authentically and appropriately to motivate, encourage, and reduce stigma for patients.
  • Support patients in identifying and pursuing personal recovery goals, building on individual strengths and resiliency.
  • Assist patients with community networking, resource navigation, and bridging to community supports and services.
  • Advocate with and on behalf of patients to ensure their voices are heard and their rights are upheld throughout the course of care.

Care Team Collaboration

  • Function as an active member of NorthStar’s four-person interdisciplinary Care Team, participating in care coordination, team huddles, and collaborative treatment planning.
  • Communicate patient needs, observations, and concerns to the clinical team in a timely, professional manner, maintaining appropriate boundaries and confidentiality.
  • Align all peer support activities with the patient’s identified treatment plan, as developed and updated by the clinical team.
  • Contribute to the organization’s quality improvement efforts by providing input on peer support service design, delivery, and outcomes.

Organizational Engagement

  • Use your lived experience voice to inform NS’s ongoing efforts to improve care quality and reduce systemic harm in behavioral health treatment.
  • Participate in mandatory orientation and ongoing training programs, including training on peer support principles, HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality, trauma-informed care, harm reduction, and NorthStar’s clinical technology platforms.
  • Attend and contribute to organizational meetings, staff development activities, and peer workforce engagement initiatives.
  • Maintain a flexible schedule including availability for evening, weekend, and holiday coverage as operationally required.

Documentation and Compliance

  • Complete timely and accurate documentation of peer support contacts, group sessions, and patient interactions in accordance with NorthStar’s Clinical Documentation Policy.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality of patient information in compliance with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2 (SUD-specific confidentiality protections), and applicable state laws.
  • Adhere to NorthStar’s Code of Conduct, Ethics and Corporate Compliance Policy, and peer-specific ethical boundaries as outlined in organizational policy.
  • Report concerns related to patient safety, critical incidents, or compliance issues through established reporting channels.

Requirements

    • Lived Experience: Personal lived experience with Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) and/or Substance Use Disorder diagnosis and/or treatment. This is a non-negotiable foundational requirement of the Peer Guide role.
    • Commitment to Harm Reduction: Demonstrated support for a harm reduction philosophy, including an all-paths-to-recovery approach, and respect for patient autonomy and self-determination.
    • Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to engage empathetically and effectively in a remote environment.
    • Technology Proficiency: Demonstrated comfort with or strong interest in virtual engagement tools, including video conferencing platforms, mobile applications, and virtual reality technologies.
    • Reliability and Flexibility: Ability to maintain a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, and to respond consistently to patient engagement expectations.

Preferred

    • Certification as a Peer Specialist, Recovery Coach, or equivalent credential recognized at the state or national level (e.g., Certified Peer Specialist, CCAR Recovery Coach).
    • Formal training or coursework in peer support principles including mutuality, self-determination, healing in relationship, and recovery-oriented systems of care
    • Lived experience as a Veteran, or experience providing peer support to Veterans or military-affiliated individuals.
    • Bilingual proficiency in Spanish and English.
    • Experience in a remote, telehealth, or technology-forward healthcare setting.

Background Check

  • All offers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of a background check in accordance with NorthStar’s Staff Background Checks and Exclusion Checks Policy and applicable state requirements. A criminal record (CORI) does not automatically disqualify candidates from consideration for this role. NS evaluates criminal history on an individualized, job-related basis.
  • Working Conditions
    • Environment: 100% remote; employees must maintain a private, professional workspace suitable for confidential patient interaction via telehealth and virtual reality platforms.
    • Schedule: Full-time (40 hours/week). Schedules include evening and weekend hours. Specific schedules are determined in coordination with the CSO.
    • Technology Requirements: Reliable high-speed internet connection, webcam-equipped computer, and ability to operate VR hardware (training provided). NS provides relevant software access.
    • Physical Demands: Primarily sedentary work performed at a computer workstation. May involve extended periods of screen use.

Benefits

  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick Leave, and Public Holidays)
  • Training and Professional Development
  • Work From Home
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) — see HR for current program details
  • Additional benefits as outlined in the NorthStar Care Employee Handbook

title: CONTROL ROOM OPERATOR
description:
FLSA STATUS: Non-Exempt


PAY RANGE: $42,378.00 - $70,630.00


REPORTS TO: Maintenance Supervisor II


DIVISION: Hydroelectric


WORK LOCATION: Seguin, Texas


SUMMARY

This position provides remote monitoring and operations via a computerized supervisory control and data acquisition system (SCADA) of raw water delivery systems, water facilities, wastewater facilities, and the hydroelectric generation system. Personnel in this position will monitor the phones and handle GBRA customer calls when necessary.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Maintain river flow calculations and convert them to an efficient operating schedule for the hydro electric generators.
  • Maintain accurate, specific and detailed daily log sheets, station and plant comparison readings, monthly reports, and environmental logs and generation spreadsheets.
  • Continually monitor lake elevations, hydroelectric plants, wastewater treatment plants, raw water delivery systems and other GBRA operations. Recognize abnormalities and perform operations as required.
  • Notify electricians, on-call personnel, and/or other team members when problems arise that must be corrected immediately. Accurately, record all information regarding such situations including times of occurrence and calls made on the daily log for future reference. Report these problems as well as any unusual conditions to the appropriate manager.
  • During times of inclement weather, Implement the GBRA “Heavy Rainfall and Flood Response” manual, monitor weather forecasts, river flows and lake elevations. Notify all necessary personnel in a timely manner in order for them to safely respond to the current situation.
  • Be able to communicate by Phone, Email, and/or Text during high river flow events and accurately record flow data and spill gate positions.
  • Record stream flow reports from upstream observers when flooding occurs.
  • Answer telephone calls after normal business hours, weekends, and holidays and possess customer service skills necessary to deal with calls from the public and customers.
  • Monitor building and facilities security after normal business hours, weekends, and holidays via closed circuit television. Notify law enforcement agencies if necessary.
  • Perform all work complying with the GBRA safety manual and policies.
  • Perform other tasks as assigned.

title: Senior Data Engineer
location: Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
description:
About Rapsodo

Rapsodo is a Sports Technology company with offices in the USA, Singapore, Turkey, Malaysia & Japan. We build data-driven sports analytics products used by athletes worldwide — from Major League Baseball players to golf enthusiasts — and by the coaches who train them. We are looking for team players who will help us deliver state-of-the-art solutions as part of Team Rapsodo.

Overview

As a senior Data & AI Engineer at Rapsodo, you will own the data platform that powers analytics, reporting, and decision-making across the company — and you will drive development of the agentic workflows built on top of it. This is a data engineer's role first: the custodianship of a production-grade warehouse spanning multiple domains, a multi-layer star schema, and a BI platform serving users company-wide. On top of that foundation, you will lead the design and delivery of agentic workflows that turn trusted data into informed, reliable action.

What You’ll Do

Own and Operate the Cloud Data Platform

  • Maintain cloud analytics infrastructure as code, treating the IaC repository as the source of truth for every cloud resource.
  • Operate a modern data stack spanning workflow orchestration, container management, ingestion, BI, and serverless compute; lead upgrades and patches with minimal disruption.
  • Operate the company-wide BI platform, including SSO integration and supporting dashboard workflows at scale.
  • Optimize warehouse cost and performance through partitioning, clustering, and query tuning; set up alerting across pipelines, connectors, and scheduled queries.
  • Enforce least-privilege access, rotate credentials on schedule, maintain backups, and keep warehouse documentation current.
  • Act as the final word on data quality and trust — every agent, dashboard, or automated workflow built on the warehouse is only as reliable as the custodianship behind it.

Build and Evolve Data Pipelines & Integrations

  • Develop transformation repositories on a multi-layer (raw → staging → curated) star schema, with incremental hash-based loading that keeps refreshes performant on very large datasets.
  • Author and maintain orchestration DAGs covering ingestion, transformation, retries, scheduling, and alerting; diagnose incidents with strong root-cause discipline.
  • Build and maintain ingestion for real-time and batch sources — database CDC, ERP, identity provider syncs, and SaaS connectors across e-commerce, payments, support, marketing, and marketplaces.
  • Lead new ingestion projects end-to-end (e.g. product event analytics, device telemetry) and drive the design of a unified semantic layer across product, CRM, billing, marketing, and support data — the layer that both humans and agents will query against.

Drive Agentic Workflow Development

  • Own the roadmap for AI agents built on top of the data warehouse — deciding which workflows justify an agent, what "grounded and trustworthy" means for each, and how they're deployed and monitored.
  • Design and build production agentic systems that read and act on warehouse data, complementing business workflows and adding value.
  • Architect end-to-end AI app stacks — serverless backends, LLM integrations, RAG, SQL generation, tool-calling/agentic orchestration, memory and context management — with access controls, evaluation harnesses, and accuracy safeguards appropriate to customer-facing use.
  • Establish engineering standards for agentic development at Rapsodo: observability (logging, tracing, quality monitoring) for AI systems, cost/latency-aware model and fallback strategy, safe and repeatable CI/CD for AI services, and guardrails against hallucination or unsafe autonomous action.
  • Push the organization's use of the warehouse forward — identify where an agent, a reporting dashboard or another solution, is the right answer to a business problem, and make the case for it.

Partner with Stakeholders and the Team

  • Support stakeholder reporting across Product, Sales, Support, Engineering, and leadership; own quarterly business processes that depend on the warehouse (e.g. commission calculations) in partnership with Sales and Finance.
  • Validate ingested data against business sources and lead investigations into discrepancies until they are resolved — the same rigor applies whether the consumer is a dashboard or an agent.
  • Manage data team and support other departments.
  • Document architectures, runbooks, agent evaluation results, and incident learnings; contribute to engineering standards across code review, testing, and release processes.

Requirements

Requirements

  • 6+ years in data engineering, analytics engineering, or platform engineering, with meaningful ownership of production systems and warehouse architecture end-to-end. Deep, hands-on data engineering experience is non-negotiable — this role leads with data custodianship, not AI engineering alone.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and shipping production AI agent systems — tool-calling architectures, RAG pipelines, context/memory orchestration, and evaluation frameworks — experience beyond prototyping with an LLM API is a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline; master's a plus.
  • Strong hands-on experience with a major cloud data platform (e.g. GCP, AWS, or Azure) — managed compute, serverless functions, container workloads — and Infrastructure-as-Code tooling.
  • Deep proficiency in SQL and Python; experience with a SQL transformation framework (Dataform, dbt, or equivalent) and container orchestration (Kubernetes or equivalent).
  • Experience building ingestion pipelines — batch and real-time (e.g. CDC) — and integrating SaaS sources with proper credential hygiene; familiarity with BI platforms and supporting non-technical users at scale.
  • Experience optimizing warehouse cost and performance on high-volume event data (partitioning, clustering, query tuning).
  • Practical experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Claude, or similar), vector databases/embedding pipelines, and evaluating LLM quality, hallucinations, and failure modes in production.
  • A track record of making the call on when an AI agent is — and isn't — the right solution to a business problem, and owning that decision through to a reliable, monitored production system.
  • Strong security mindset; comfort partnering with business stakeholders on cross-functional deliverables; excellent communication, documentation, and ownership in fast-paced environments.
  • Interest in sports technology is a plus.

Benefits

Why Rapsodo?

At Rapsodo, you won't just build agents on someone else's data platform — you'll own the platform itself and decide how AI gets built on top of it. This role is built for someone who wants both: the discipline of being the trusted custodian of a company's data, and the license to drive where agentic AI takes the organization next. If you want to shape both the foundation and the frontier, apply now.

title: Director of Secondary Market & Unit Management
description:
Kaizen is looking for an experienced Director of Secondary Market & Unit Management to lead our secondary market strategy, drive property transaction volume, optimize unit portfolio performance, and deliver sustainable revenue and asset value growth. This role goes beyond traditional sales management the Director will shape and execute the secondary market commercial strategy, end-to-end unit lifecycle management, strengthen stakeholder relationships, and align operations with Kaizen’s long-term business objectives. You will lead a high-performing team, nurture B2C client relationships, and collaborate cross-functionally to deliver seamless property transactions, superior unit performance, and exceptional client experiences.

Key Responsibilities

Secondary Market & Unit Portfolio Performance

  • Develop and execute secondary market strategies for resales, off-plan resales, leasing, and unit disposition — driving transaction volume, market share, and revenue
  • Own end-to-end unit portfolio management: inventory oversight, valuation, pricing, marketing readiness, and lifecycle optimization from listing to close
  • Maximize asset value, minimize holding periods, and optimize yield through data-driven pricing, targeted promotion, and timely disposition
  • Monitor UAE/GCC market trends, supply-demand dynamics, regulatory updates, and competitor activity to inform pricing and positioning

B2C Growth & Platform Services

  • Build, scale, and optimize a partner-led service marketplace; onboard, manage, and assure quality across provider networks
  • Leverage existing developer, property manager, and owner relationships to accelerate growth ahead of competitors
  • Define commercial models, pricing, and service standards; oversee end-to-end client experience and recommend strategic adjustments (expand, refine, or pivot) based on performance

Client, Stakeholder & Relationship Management

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with individual homeowners, buyers, tenants, investors, developers, brokers, and institutional partners
  • Drive client retention, repeat business, and referrals through proactive engagement, transparent communication, and personalized guidance
  • Lead commercial negotiations, valuations, listing agreements, tenders, and complex transactions — tailoring solutions to individual client needs
  • Represent Kaizen as a market expert; uphold service excellence and trust across all client interactions

Operational Excellence & Process Leadership

  • Establish clear KPIs, accountability frameworks, and reporting standards across transactions, listings, portfolio performance, and client satisfaction
  • Continuously refine end-to-end journeys — from inquiry → consultation → valuation → transaction → post-closing support & services
  • Leverage CRM, analytics, valuation tools, and digital solutions to boost productivity, market intelligence, and client engagement

People Leadership & Culture

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team across secondary market sales, unit management, and B2C services
  • Set clear objectives, coach for results, and nurture expertise in transaction excellence, B2C relationship-building, and service delivery
  • Foster a collaborative, client-first, high-performance culture; role-model Kaizen’s values and leadership standards

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Real Estate, or related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred
  • Significant leadership experience in secondary market sales, property transactions, portfolio management, B2C growth, or marketplace/platform businesses
  • Deep proven knowledge of the UAE/GCC real estate market, regulations, valuation practices, and transaction workflows
  • Strong B2C track record: successfully advising individual owners, buyers, and tenants; building trust, explaining complex processes clearly, and delivering high satisfaction
  • Proven ability to grow revenue, optimize portfolios, and scale service lines with measurable results
  • Experience building partner ecosystems, marketplace models, or platform-led services

title: Senior Cloud Architect (6-month Contract)
description:
Senior Cloud Architect – CONTRACT – 6 months

Department: Tech & IS
Service Group: Project Business Operations
Reports to: Director, Information Systems
Location: MEMS Calgary or Sherwood Park offices

About the Role

Millennium EMS Solutions Ltd. is seeking a Senior Cloud Architect to lead the design, governance, security, optimization, and operational excellence of our cloud and hybrid technology environments. This role is responsible for ensuring MEMS’ cloud services are secure, resilient, scalable, cost-effective, and aligned with business objectives while supporting modernization and digital transformation initiatives.

The Senior Cloud Architect will play a key role in shaping MEMS’ cloud strategy, with a primary focus on Microsoft Azure and the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. Working closely with Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Applications, and Business teams, this position will establish technical standards, strengthen cloud governance, improve operational reliability, and support solutions that enhance agility, security, business continuity, service delivery, and cost efficiency.

This is a contract opportunity for an experienced cloud professional who enjoys combining hands-on technical expertise with strategic architecture, enterprise governance, automation, and continuous improvement.

What You’ll Do

In this role, you will:

  • Develop and maintain cloud architecture strategies aligned with MEMS’ organizational and technology roadmaps.
  • Design scalable, secure, resilient, and high-performing cloud solutions using Microsoft Azure and hybrid infrastructure platforms.
  • Establish cloud standards, reference architectures, and technical governance frameworks.
  • Lead the deployment, administration, and ongoing management of cloud infrastructure services.
  • Monitor cloud environments and proactively identify opportunities to improve performance, reliability, security, and cost efficiency.
  • Lead troubleshooting and resolution of cloud infrastructure incidents and service disruptions.
  • Design and administer Microsoft Entra ID identity and access management, including authentication, authorization, privileged access, and identity governance controls.
  • Implement and maintain Zero Trust security principles across cloud environments.
  • Lead cloud security controls, vulnerability reviews, remediation planning, and security posture improvements.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain cloud governance standards, policies, operating procedures, and documentation.
  • Build and maintain automation frameworks using Infrastructure as Code and repeatable deployment methodologies.
  • Support CI/CD initiatives, automation, standardization, and operational efficiency improvements.
  • Provide advanced administration and support for Microsoft 365 services and related cloud collaboration platforms.
  • Design, test, and maintain backup, disaster recovery, failover, and business continuity capabilities.
  • Monitor cloud consumption, licensing utilization, operational spending, and vendor performance.
  • Support cloud modernization, migration, and digital transformation initiatives.

What You Bring

The successful candidate will bring a strong blend of enterprise cloud architecture, infrastructure, security, governance, and collaboration skills. Qualifications include:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of progressive IT infrastructure experience.
  • 6+ years of enterprise Azure administration or architecture experience.
  • Experience supporting hybrid cloud and on-premises environments.
  • Experience implementing enterprise cloud security controls.
  • Experience administering Microsoft 365 services.
  • Experience with SAST, DAST, and penetration testing applications for Azure applications.

Technical Skills and Experience

We are looking for experience with several of the following:

  • Microsoft Azure infrastructure and platform services
  • Azure networking, compute, storage, backup, and disaster recovery services
  • Microsoft Entra ID, identity and access management, Conditional Access, MFA, SSO, RBAC, and PIM
  • Microsoft Defender Suite, Microsoft Sentinel, and Microsoft Purview
  • Microsoft 365 administration, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, and Intune
  • Infrastructure as Code, including Terraform, Bicep, and ARM templates
  • PowerShell, Azure CLI, Azure DevOps, and CI/CD pipelines
  • Virtualization technologies such as VMware and Hyper-V
  • Enterprise networking, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, routing, firewalls, and load balancing
  • Cloud governance, cost management, security monitoring, SIEM, vulnerability management, and Zero Trust architecture
  • Storage, backup, and disaster recovery solutions.

Preferred Certifications

One or more of the following certifications would be considered an asset:

  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert, AZ-305
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate, AZ-104
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate, AZ-500
  • Microsoft Certified: Cybersecurity Architect Expert, SC-100
  • Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator, SC-300
  • CISSP

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role will be measured by the ability to maintain reliable, secure, well-governed, and cost-effective cloud services while enabling modernization and operational excellence across MEMS. Key outcomes include maintaining critical cloud service availability, resolving incidents within established service levels, strengthening cloud security and compliance, increasing the use of approved Infrastructure as Code methodologies, completing annual disaster recovery testing, maintaining cloud spend within approved budget parameters, and delivering cloud projects on time and within budget.

Working at MEMS

At MEMS, we are committed to fostering a culture grounded in our core values of Service, Quality, Trust, Innovation, and Teamwork. The Senior Cloud Architect will contribute to this culture by delivering secure, reliable, and forward-looking cloud solutions that support our people, our clients, and our continued growth.

This position is based in a professional office environment and involves regular use of computers, office technology, and virtual collaboration tools. Occasional travel to MEMS offices or project sites may be required, and the role may involve extended hours or varying shifts during critical project milestones.

Why Join MEMS?

This is a high-impact opportunity to help shape the future of MEMS’ cloud and hybrid technology environment. You will work across technical and business teams to strengthen security, improve reliability, modernize systems, enable automation, and support the digital capabilities that help MEMS deliver quality service to our clients.

How to Apply

If you are a strategic and hands-on cloud professional with deep Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 expertise, we encourage you to apply for the Contract, Senior Cloud Architect opportunity with MEMS. This is a 6 month contract duration with the possibility to extend or convert to a permanent role.

Please submit your resume and cover letter outlining your experience with enterprise cloud architecture, cloud security, automation, governance, and Microsoft cloud technologies.

title: 1st Shift Direct Care
description:
Position Summary

As a Residential Support Specialist, you will provide a supportive and safe environment in community residential settings within MHA’s ICL (Integrated Community Living) department. This role involves traveling to different program locations based on staffing needs, offering flexibility and consistent support across the department. You will help foster growth, independence, and community engagement for individuals who have experienced a brain injury resulting in physical limitations, mental health, and/or cognitive challenges.

Pay Range: $19 - $21 an hour

Open Shift: Saturday & Sunday 9am-3pm (12hrs)

- TWO POSITIONS OPEN

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide respectful, person-centered support to participants in daily living activities, personal care, and skill development.
  • Promote community integration by facilitating access to transportation, social activities, and external resources.
  • Support participants' health needs, including medication administration (per MAP standards), appointment scheduling, and monitoring overall wellbeing.
  • Assist with financial skills and money management, maintaining accurate documentation of all expenditures.
  • Respond to emergencies and crisis situations appropriately, following agency protocols and communicating with supervisors.
  • Advocate for participants and help them build self-advocacy skills; serve as a liaison with families, providers, and community supports.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of Individual Service Plans (ISPs), documenting progress and participation.
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation, including daily logs, incident reports, and health records.
  • Promote a safe environment by following all safety procedures, assisting with emergency drills, and identifying potential hazards.
  • Collaborate effectively with team members, attend training, maintain certifications (MAP, CPR, First Aid), and actively participate in meetings and supervision.

About Integration & Community Living (ICL)

The Integration & Community Living (ICL) program supports individuals with developmental disabilities and brain injuries in living independently and meaningfully in the community. In partnership with the Department of Developmental Services (DDS), ICL provides person-centered residential and outreach services across Western Massachusetts. With over 60 years of experience, MHA helps individuals transition from institutional settings into homes where they can grow, make choices, and fully participate in community life. Services range from supported and shared living to emergency respite and privately funded care, all designed to promote independence, dignity, and connection.

Equal Opportunity Statement

The Mental Health Association is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Requirements

  • Valid driver’s license and an acceptable driving record.
  • Strong communication, organizational, and computer skills.
  • Adaptability to participants' changing needs.
  • Provide personal care, including assistance with bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and mobility.
  • Ability to pass and maintain certifications in medication administration (MAP), CPR, and First Aid.
  • Must be at least 18 years old.
  • High school diploma or GED required; college degree in human services or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of six months of relevant experience; experience with individuals with brain injuries, mental health challenges, or developmental disabilities is preferred.

title: Intermediate Hydrogeologist
description:
The Intermediate Hydrogeologist supports the delivery of hydrogeological, groundwater supply, contaminated sites, and resource-sector projects within MEMS' Water Resources Service Group. The role applies strong technical expertise and project execution skills to plan and conduct hydrogeological investigations, groundwater monitoring programs, aquifer testing, groundwater supply assessments, and contaminated site assessments across municipal, industrial, energy, and natural resource sectors.

Working with moderate independence, the Intermediate Hydrogeologist leads technical components of projects, including field program execution, data interpretation, conceptual site model development, hydrogeological assessments, and technical reporting. The position contributes to successful project delivery through effective management of scope, schedule, quality, and safety requirements while supporting positive client outcomes.

The successful candidate will have experience in one or more of groundwater supply, contaminated sites, oil and gas, mining, or environmental assessment projects. Experience with groundwater flow and contaminant transport modeling, including MODFLOW, is considered a strong asset. The role also supports business growth through client relationship development, proposal preparation, collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, and mentoring of junior staff, while upholding MEMS' core values of Service, Quality, Trust, Innovation, and Teamwork.

Please note this position may be based out of our Sherwood Park or Calgary office.

Key Accountabilities

Project Delivery and Technical Execution

  • Lead and execute technical components of hydrogeological projects, including groundwater supply assessments, aquifer testing programs, groundwater licensing, contaminated sites investigations, and resource-sector projects.
  • Plan, coordinate, and oversee field programs including drilling, monitoring well installation, groundwater monitoring, sampling, and hydraulic testing.
  • Support project managers in delivering projects within scope, schedule, budget, quality, and safety requirements.
  • Coordinate field contractors and subcontractors to ensure efficient and safe project execution.

Hydrogeological Assessment, Data Interpretation, and Modelling

  • Analyze hydrogeological, hydrogeochemical, and environmental datasets to characterize groundwater systems and support project objectives.
  • Develop and refine conceptual site models to evaluate groundwater flow, aquifer characteristics, contaminant migration, and water resource availability.
  • Conduct quantitative hydrogeological analyses and assessments to support regulatory, engineering, environmental, and operational decisions.
  • Apply groundwater flow and contaminant transport modelling tools, including MODFLOW or equivalent software, where appropriate.

Technical Reporting and Regulatory Support

  • Prepare and review high-quality technical reports, work plans, and client deliverables.
  • Support regulatory applications, permitting activities, groundwater licensing, environmental assessments, and compliance reporting.
  • Present technical findings, conclusions, and recommendations clearly to clients, regulators, and multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Ensure all technical work meets applicable regulatory requirements, industry standards, and MEMS quality expectations.

Client Service and Business Growth

  • Build and maintain positive working relationships with clients through responsive communication and successful project delivery.
  • Identify opportunities to support clients across groundwater supply, contaminated sites, oil and gas, mining, and water resource projects.
  • Contribute to proposal preparation, scopes of work, cost estimates, and technical approaches for new opportunities.
  • Support the continued growth of MEMS' hydrogeology and water resources practice, particularly within the mining sector.

Team Collaboration, Mentorship, and Continuous Improvement

  • Collaborate effectively with hydrogeologists, engineers, geoscientists, environmental specialists, and other technical professionals.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior staff during field and office-based activities.
  • Promote a strong culture of safety, quality, innovation, and teamwork.
  • Maintain awareness of emerging industry practices, regulations, technologies, and modelling approaches to enhance technical excellence and client service.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Geoscience (Hydrogeology, Geological Engineering) or related discipline.
  • Minimum 5–10 years of relevant experience in hydrogeology or contaminated sites consulting.
  • Eligibility for professional designation (e.g., P.Geo., P.Eng.) required.
  • Experience with field programs, pumping test programs, groundwater monitoring, and data interpretation.
  • Valid Class 5 Driver’s License (non-GDL).

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Strong understanding of hydrogeological principles, groundwater flow systems, and contaminant transport
  • Ability to solve aquifer tests using analytical methods
  • Knowledge of Alberta Water Act and other associated provincial guidelines and regulations for licensing of groundwater supplies
  • Familiarity with any other applicable provincial regulations and environmental standards
  • Knowledge of the geology and depositional environments of the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin.
  • Familiarity of contaminated site assessment practices in Canada
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and standard technical reporting tools
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills

Working Conditions:

  • This role is primarily office based. However, some field work or travel to client sites may be required on a project-specific basis with each trip lasting anywhere from 1 to 10 days. This individual may conduct work at industrial or commercial facilities, brownfield sites and/or greenfield sites in varying locations (remote to urban). In some cases, the field work may include carrying sampling equipment.
  • Office environment that requires sitting for extended periods of time.
  • Prolonged exposure to computer keyboards and computer screens.
  • Manual dexterity required to use desktop computer and peripherals.
  • Sometimes requires long hours of work. Occasional interruptions outside work hours and travel to other locations are required.
  • Ability to work varying shifts.
  • Required to walk, stand, climb, bend forward, kneel down, crawl, reach and grasp, push and pull objects, lift and/or move up to 30 kg, sometimes over the shoulders, repetitive bending and lifting of items, along with repetitive arm movements.

About MEMS

Millennium EMS Solutions Ltd. (MEMS) is an employee-owned environmental consultancy providing environmental, health and engineering services across western Canada since 1998. We are known for our credibility, integrity, technical competence, and our talented staff. We meet and exceed the needs of our client’s projects because we are prepared technically, professionally, and logistically. We are delivery-oriented and deliver superior, cost-effective services.

Why Choose MEMS?

MEMS believes in supporting employees in achieving their career goals while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. In addition to rewarding job opportunities, we offer an attractive employee package, including:

title: PORTER
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Porter supports safe, clean, organized, and efficient shop operations by cleaning and detailing fusion equipment, maintaining work areas, organizing equipment and materials, and providing general assistance to shop personnel. This is an entry-level, hands-on shop-support position performed primarily in shop, warehouse, equipment-storage, and yard environments under the direction of the Shop Supervisor.

The Porter helps maintain equipment readiness and appearance, supports basic equipment preparation and maintenance activities within the employee’s training and authorization, assists with loading and movement of equipment, and maintains assigned shop and yard areas in a professional condition. The position requires a strong safety mindset, reliability, teamwork, attention to detail, and willingness to perform physically active work in varying environmental conditions.

The Porter may occasionally support deliveries, pickups, inter-branch movement, or customer/job-site assignments as business needs require. Success in this role depends on safe work practices, care of company equipment and assets, prompt reporting of unsafe or damaged equipment, and consistent support of shop and branch operations.

EQUIPMENT CLEANING, DETAILING & SHOP SUPPORT

1. Clean, wash, detail, and prepare fusion equipment, tools, vehicles, shop equipment, and related company assets using approved methods and products.

2. Maintain shop floors, work areas, storage areas, equipment locations, and surrounding shop and yard areas in a clean, safe, and organized condition.

3. Assist shop personnel by supplying, holding, staging, or moving tools, materials, parts, and equipment as directed.

4. Clean and lubricate equipment within the employee’s training, assigned duties, and authorization.

5. Assist with basic equipment preparation, setup, inspection, or maintenance activities after receiving appropriate training and authorization.

6. Identify and promptly report damaged, unsafe, leaking, missing, incomplete, or improperly stored equipment to the Shop Supervisor or designated representative.

7. Maintain equipment, tools, materials, and shop assets in designated locations and assist with tracking their location and movement.

8. Perform authorized cosmetic equipment preparation, including touch-up painting of faded, chipped, or worn surfaces.

9. Safely operate basic hand tools, power tools, pressure-washing equipment, cleaning equipment, and other approved shop tools after required training.

10. Assist with loading, unloading, staging, positioning, and moving equipment and materials when trained and authorized.

11. Maintain clean and orderly product displays, shelves, parts areas, workstations, equipment areas, and other assigned spaces.

12. Perform routine housekeeping duties, including sweeping, cleaning, trash removal, spill cleanup, and general shop organization.

13. Support inventory, equipment-location, shop-organization, and equipment-readiness activities as assigned.

SAFETY, EQUIPMENT OPERATION & ASSET PROTECTION

1. Follow all applicable Milford, Winsupply, customer-specific, and shop safety policies, procedures, PPE requirements, equipment rules, and safe work practices.

2. Follow applicable chemical labels, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), PPE requirements, ventilation requirements, and approved procedures when using cleaning products, paints, coatings, lubricants, fuels, solvents, or other shop materials.

3. Obtain and maintain Milford-required forklift and telehandler operator qualification/certification within 90 days of employment unless a documented business-need exception is approved by management. Employees may not operate this equipment until required training is completed and company authorization is received.

4. Perform required pre-use inspections of forklifts, telehandlers, pressure-washing equipment, power tools, vehicles, and other assigned equipment and promptly report defects or unsafe conditions.

5. Do not use equipment, tools, chemicals, or machinery for which the employee has not been trained or authorized.

6. Immediately report injuries, spills, near misses, property damage, unsafe conditions, equipment damage, missing equipment, or suspected misuse of company assets.

7. Protect company vehicles, equipment, tools, materials, inventory, fuel, keys, access devices, and other assets from loss, damage, misuse, or unauthorized use.

8. Follow approved procedures for spill response, waste disposal, housekeeping, storage of chemicals and materials, and removal of damaged or unsafe equipment from use.

DRIVING, DELIVERIES & CUSTOMER-SITE SUPPORT

1. Operate company vehicles as assigned to move equipment, pick up parts or supplies, make deliveries, support inter-branch needs, or complete other approved business activities.

2. Assist with safe loading, unloading, positioning, and securement of equipment, parts, tools, and materials for transport when trained and authorized.

3. Travel to customer or job sites occasionally when business needs require and comply with all applicable customer, site-access, safety, PPE, badging, training, and testing requirements.

4. Represent Milford professionally when interacting with customers, vendors, other branches, and members of the public during assigned driving or support activities.

5. Promptly report vehicle, cargo, equipment, delivery, customer-site, or safety concerns to the Shop Supervisor or designated management representative.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Communicate effectively with the Shop Supervisor, shop personnel, Technical Services, Warehouse, Rental, Operations, and other departments as needed to support safe and efficient work.

2. Maintain reliable attendance and punctuality and remain available during assigned work hours and required extended-hour or weekend assignments.

3. Complete required training, inspections, checklists, equipment records, and other documentation accurately and on time.

4. Ask for guidance when uncertain about an assigned task, equipment condition, safe work method, chemical use, customer-site requirement, or other matter outside the employee’s training or authorization.

5. Perform other duties as assigned by the Shop Supervisor or designated management representative.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS

1. Ability and willingness to perform physically active shop, warehouse, yard, and equipment-support work.

2. Ability to follow written and verbal instructions, established work procedures, safety requirements, chemical labels, and equipment instructions.

3. Basic mechanical aptitude and ability to safely use hand tools, power tools, cleaning equipment, and shop equipment after training.

4. Good communication, organization, teamwork, reliability, and attention-to-detail skills.

5. Ability to identify unsafe equipment, damaged assets, leaks, spills, or unsafe work conditions and report concerns promptly.

6. Ability to maintain a professional and cooperative working relationship with supervisors, coworkers, customers, vendors, and other departments.

7. Ability to prioritize assigned tasks and adapt to changing shop, equipment, customer, or business needs.

8. Ability to safely operate company vehicles and maintain required driving qualifications.

9. Ability to complete and maintain required safety, equipment, driving, customer-site, and job-specific training within established timeframes.

10. Ability to read, write, speak, and understand English sufficiently to safely perform assigned duties, understand safety information, labels, SDS information, instructions, and required documentation.

11. Ability to maintain confidentiality regarding customer information, company records, equipment information, and other sensitive business matters.

title: Acute Care Worker
description:
Position Summary

The ACT staff performs a variety of duties to provide necessary supports to individuals with developmental disabilities, intellectual disabilities, brain injuries, mental health issues, and/or substance abuse disorders to enable independent living in the community. Perform responsibilities professionally and collaboratively in accordance with MHA’s Core Values (Respect, Integrity, and Compassion), policies, funding requirements, and regulatory guidelines.

Pay Range: $19 - $21 an hour

Open Shift: Monday 1pm-3pm, Friday 11am-9pm, Saturday & Sunday 7am-9pm (40hrs)

Key Responsibilities

  • Teach and model independent living skills such as budgeting, cooking, cleaning, and social interaction to support participant growth and self-sufficiency.
  • Serve as an advocate and liaison for participants with landlords, healthcare providers, social services, and family members.
  • Provide transportation to appointments, social activities, and other essential engagements while maintaining a reliable, work-ready vehicle.
  • Offer on-call support during scheduled, overnight, and holiday hours, responding promptly to medical and psychiatric emergencies.
  • Respond to crises by ensuring participant safety, providing support, and coordinating emergency services when necessary.
  • Administer medications in accordance with MAP standards, including monitoring health status and documenting all administration and vital signs.
  • Track, manage, and maintain medication systems, including refills, documentation, error reporting, and disposal procedures.
  • Maintain accurate, timely documentation including daily notes, incident reports, medication records, and appointment tracking.
  • Ensure a safe, clean, and well-stocked environment, including office upkeep and conducting safety checks.
  • Collaborate with team members and participate in trainings and meetings while maintaining effective communication with participants, families, and providers.

About Integration & Community Living (ICL)

The Integration & Community Living (ICL) program supports individuals with developmental disabilities and brain injuries in living independently and meaningfully in the community. In partnership with the Department of Developmental Services (DDS), ICL provides person-centered residential and outreach services across Western Massachusetts. With over 60 years of experience, MHA helps individuals transition from institutional settings into homes where they can grow, make choices, and fully participate in community life. Services range from supported and shared living to emergency respite and privately funded care, all designed to promote independence, dignity, and connection.

Equal Opportunity Statement

The Mental Health Association is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Requirements

  • Valid driver’s license, reliable insured vehicle, acceptable driving record, and ability to complete driver training.
  • Strong oral, written, computer, and organizational skills.
  • Adaptability to changing participant needs and program requirements.
  • Certified in MAP with medication administration experience; able to pass CPR and First Aid certifications.
  • Must be at least 18 years old.
  • High school diploma or GED required; college degree in human services or related field preferred.
  • At least six months of relevant experience supporting individuals with developmental/intellectual disabilities and/or mental health issues, including MAP medication administration.

Benefits

  • Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
  • Retirement Plan (403B, IRA)
  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)
  • Family Leave (Maternity, Paternity)
  • Long Term Disability
  • $19-$21 an hour

title: Advisor with Deep Hedge Funds Connections
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
About the job

You'd advise the CEO directly: a monthly call where your job is to tell him where he's wrong, plus make warm introductions to people at funds you think we should be talking to. Expect to make about five introductions a month, more in the first month as we get going. We care far more about talking to the right five than a bigger number of intros. A few hours a month. NOTE: this is a contract consulting role, not a part time employment role.

We believe the fundamental investing firms of the future will run on data infrastructure and workflow tools built for how they actually work. The payoff is sharper thinking, more coverage per analyst, and ultimately more alpha. We built Mercata inside a $600M long/short that has paid for it in production since April, and that fund's COO and CIO also invested in the company directly. We're looking for advisors who hold the same level of conviction about the future.

About Mercata

Mercata is a hedge fund's brain. Fundamental investing hedge funds are full of brilliant people who can't remember what they know when it counts, so we built the firm's memory: not just the records like an RMS, but the reasoning that produced them - the debates, the objections, the names the team passed on - all of it linked to the filings, news, and market data moving every day. The memo keeps the decision; Mercata keeps what produced it. Because it sits in the research flow, every question the team asks becomes part of the firm's memory, and the longer it runs, the smarter the firm becomes. Everything it says is citable back to a source. Think of it as the tireless associate who has been in every meeting, hears everything, and forgets nothing.

Requirements

  • 10 years of experience as a COO, CIO, or PM inside a $500M+ fundamental investing hedge fund
  • A network of COOs and CIOs at established $50M-$2B funds who are likely to take your calls
  • Unrestricted from working with Mercata. Independent, retired, or running your own shop.
  • Genuine conviction that the fundamental investing firms of the future will run on infrastructure like this

Benefits

Equity: a meaningful advisor grant vesting monthly over two years. Exact numbers on the first call.

This is not an employment role and as such, there are no employee benefits offered.

title: Engineering Manager - DevOps
description:
LiveData Explained

Engineering Manager - Dev Ops

LiveData | Remote, United States (Eastern Time preferred) | Full-Time

Why LiveData

LiveData builds cloud-based surgical software that helps hospitals run operating rooms more efficiently while improving patient outcomes. The systems behind this work must be reliable, secure, observable, and cost-aware.

This role leads the DevOps function at LiveData, managing a small team of two engineers while staying close to the technical work. You will report to the VP Engineering, and own how infrastructure, deployment, operations, and reliability are designed and run across the company.

About LiveData

LiveData is a healthcare technology company automating clinical and operational workflows across Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems. We build on a serverless-first AWS architecture to keep systems lean and scalable while relying on managed services where they fit best.

LiveData was selected by Modern Healthcare as one of the Best Places to Work in Healthcare for 2026, its eighth consecutive year on the list.

The Role

We are hiring a DevOps Engineering Manager to lead and improve our DevOps function. You will manage two DevOps engineers and work closely with software engineering, QA, security, and leadership to improve delivery speed, reliability, observability, security, and AWS cost efficiency.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You are expected to make architectural decisions, review infrastructure changes, shape CI/CD workflows, guide incident response, and help solve difficult production and platform problems in a pragmatic way.

Our environment is AWS-first and serverless-first, with a strong preference for automation, infrastructure as code, and managed services over undifferentiated operational toil.

What You Will Do

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of two DevOps engineers.
  • Own the health and maturity of the DevOps function: infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, and release processes.
  • Define and execute a DevOps roadmap aligned with engineering and business goals.
  • Partner with software engineers to improve developer experience and deployment reliability.
  • Strengthen infrastructure as code, automation standards, and operational runbooks.
  • Oversee production operations: monitoring, alerting, incident response, and root cause analysis.
  • Drive reliability, availability, backup and recovery readiness, and disaster recovery planning.
  • Guide secure infrastructure and delivery practices in collaboration with security and engineering leadership.
  • Manage and optimize AWS usage with attention to scalability, resilience, and cost.
  • Track and report key operational metrics (e.g., deployment frequency, change failure rate, availability, mean time to recovery, cloud spend).
  • Help evaluate tooling and vendor choices appropriate for a small engineering organization.
  • Support future hiring and growth of the DevOps function.
  • Use AI coding assistants and automation tools as part of daily workflows.

Requirements

What You Bring

Required

  • 6+ years in DevOps, platform, SRE, or infrastructure engineering.
  • 2+ years leading engineers directly or serving as technical lead for a small DevOps/platform team.
  • Strong hands-on experience with AWS in production environments.
  • Experience building and improving CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code.
  • Proven track record operating production systems with a focus on reliability, observability, and incident response.
  • Experience with cloud security fundamentals, secrets management, identity and access control, and secure deployment practices.
  • Strong working knowledge of Linux, networking fundamentals, and shell-based troubleshooting.
  • Experience with scripting or software development in Python, Bash, or similar languages.
  • Ability to review and refine AI-generated code or configuration using sound engineering judgment.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively across engineering, leadership, and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred

  • Experience in healthcare or another regulated environment.
  • Experience with serverless AWS services such as Lambda, API Gateway, S3, CloudWatch, IAM, EventBridge, RDS, or Aurora.
  • Experience with AWS CDK, Terraform, or similar infrastructure-as-code tooling.
  • Familiarity with compliance-minded engineering practices (auditability, access review, logging and retention controls, change management).
  • Experience improving developer experience for small engineering teams.
  • Familiarity with PostgreSQL, application performance monitoring, and AWS cost optimization.
  • Experience developing MUMPS code in an Intersystems Cache/IRIS environment.
  • Experience with AI-assisted development tools and workflows.
  • Experience supporting remote engineering teams and coordinating operational work across time zones.

Tech Environment

  • Cloud: AWS (serverless-first)
  • Infrastructure: Infrastructure as code, automation-first operations
  • Data: Aurora and other relational databases
  • Development: GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, command-line tooling, AI coding assistants
  • Architecture: REST APIs, event-driven workflows, managed cloud services
  • Operations: Monitoring, alerting, logging, incident response, deployment automation

What Sets This Role Apart

  • Small-team impact. You can drive meaningful operational and platform improvements quickly.
  • Real people leadership. Direct management responsibility for two engineers.
  • Technical depth. You stay close to architecture, tooling, and production operations.
  • Healthcare context. Systems support clinical and operational workflows where uptime, traceability, and pragmatic risk management matter.
  • AI-assisted engineering. AI tooling is part of daily work, anchored by strong engineering judgment.

Benefits

Compensation

Competitive salary commensurate with experience. Benefits include generous health, dental, and vision insurance; an employer-matched 401(k); paid time off; and remote work flexibility. Based on experience and location, the target salary range for this role is $125-$175K.

Work Location

This is a remote-first role. While you can work from anywhere in the U.S., we strongly prefer candidates in the Eastern Time Zone. If you are located elsewhere, you should have experience working core business hours (8 AM to 5 PM ET). Additionally, you must be available to travel to the Boston area approximately once per quarter for in-person team collaboration.

Employment Authorization

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship now or in the future.

The chosen candidate must pass a standard background check/drug test.

title: DIMP Model Engineer
description:
Risk Model Engineer — Gas Distribution Integrity

Location: Remote (US or Canada)
Department: Insights (AI/ML)
Reports to: Data Science Team Lead

About the Role

Irth is building a new AI-driven threat and risk management platform for pipeline asset integrity. The platform brings together three capabilities that have never previously lived in one place at Irth:

  • A governed, cross-product data platform built on Databricks and Azure.
  • An AI-powered ingestion layer that normalizes, repairs, and enriches customer data without services-heavy onboarding.
  • A reusable analytical layer that runs industry-standard, Irth-developed, and customer-built risk models against that data.

We are hiring a Risk Model Engineer to own the gas distribution risk models within that analytical layer.

Distribution is a new model domain for the platform. The threat framework and model set are being defined now in collaboration with subject-matter experts and design-partner operators. In this role, you will help define the models, build them, and take them through validation—producing outputs that utilities can use to prioritize replacement programs and support regulatory proceedings.

The modeling work focuses on large populations of buried assets with relatively few observed failures, incomplete records, and limited direct inspection data. The work spans physics-based probabilistic models and machine learning, with an emphasis on producing risk rankings that remain explainable, calibrated, and defensible.

You will own the model content: what the model computes, why it computes it, and the evidence supporting its validity.

Productionization—including model serving, data pipelines, deployment, and monitoring infrastructure—is owned by dedicated ML Ops and data engineering roles with whom you will work closely.

Key Responsibilities

1. Threat Framework & Integration

  • Translate the gas distribution threat framework, in collaboration with subject-matter experts, into systematic threat identification methods and supporting data structures.
  • Integrate model inputs from diverse datasets across Irth's product offerings.
  • Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and limitations in source data and determine how they should be reflected in model inputs and outputs.

2. Model Development

  • Extend threat coverage across domains, including:
    • Legacy material corrosion
    • Plastic embrittlement
    • Excavation damage
    • Cross-bores
    • Other gas distribution

Requirements

Skills We're Hiring For

We are hiring across a broad range of capabilities and do not expect a single candidate to have all of them. We are looking for strong depth in one or more areas and the curiosity and judgment to work across the others.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Gas distribution integrity management — program design, threat identification under 49 CFR Part 192, Subpart P, and replacement prioritization, from the operator, consultancy, regulator, or technology-vendor side.
  • Legacy material risk — cast iron, bare steel, vintage plastics, and plastic embrittlement.
  • Leak survey, methane detection, and cross-bore programs.
  • Machine learning applied to physical asset data, including time-series, survival, anomaly-detection, and classification models trainer

Benefits

Benefits

  • Competitive Salary – A competitive compensation package based on experience and qualifications.
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance – Comprehensive insurance coverage to support you and your family.
  • 401(k) Plan with Company Match.
  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) – Time off to support work-life balance and personal needs.
  • Company-Paid Holidays – Paid holidays throughout the year.
  • Flexible Work Options – Work-from-home opportunities are available, depending on role and business needs.
  • On-Call Compensation – Additional pay for eligible on-call shifts.

title: Program Manager
description:
About LIDD

LIDD is a leading supply chain management consulting firm specializing in strategy, design, implementation, and optimization of supply chain operations and enterprise technology solutions. We help manufacturers, distributors, and retailers transform their operations through innovative supply chain and ERP solutions.

The Role

The Program Manager is a senior delivery leader within LIDD's Project Services Office (PSO). This role is responsible for overseeing large-scale, multi-workstream client programs while contributing to the development and continuous improvement of the PSO as a shared service across the organization.

The Program Manager provides leadership across ERP, Supply Chain Planning, Warehouse Management, Transportation Management, and Digital Transformation initiatives. They ensure delivery excellence through effective governance, resource coordination, stakeholder management, risk mitigation, and financial oversight.

In addition to managing strategic client programs, the Program Manager plays a key role in building project management standards, mentoring Project Managers, improving delivery methodologies, and supporting portfolio planning across multiple practices.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead complex enterprise software and supply chain transformation programs from initiation through post-go-live stabilization.
  • Manage multiple interconnected projects and workstreams simultaneously.
  • Establish program governance, executive steering committees, and decision-making frameworks.
  • Drive successful execution against scope, budget, schedule, quality, and business objectives.
  • Manage program dependencies, risks, critical paths, and resource constraints.
  • Serve as the senior delivery contact for executive stakeholders.
  • Lead escalation management and resolution of critical delivery issues.
  • Champion project and program management best practices across the organization.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of PSO standards, tools, templates, and governance frameworks.
  • Promote consistency while enabling flexibility across technology practices.
  • Support capacity planning, resource forecasting, and prioritization across client engagements.
  • Provide guidance on project health, risk exposure, and delivery performance.
  • Coach, mentor, and develop Project Managers and Project Coordinators.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Information Systems, Supply Chain, Operations Management, or a related discipline.
  • 6+ years of experience managing complex technology implementation programs.
  • Demonstrated experience leading large ERP or enterprise software implementations.
  • Proven success managing multi-project programs with multiple stakeholders and workstreams.
  • Strong financial management and commercial acumen.
  • Exceptional communication, leadership, and executive presentation skills.

Preferred

  • Experience with ERP platforms such as NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, Oracle, or Infor.
  • Experience in Supply Chain Planning, Warehouse Management (WMS), Transportation Management (TMS), or related technologies.
  • Experience establishing or improving PMO/PSO functions.
  • Experience leading organizational change and business transformation initiatives.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing, distribution, logistics, and retail operations.
  • 5+ years of experience in a consulting, professional services, or systems integrator environment.

Certifications

  • PMP certification considered a significant asset.
  • PgMP certification considered a significant asset.
  • Agile, Scrum, Prosci, or related certifications are advantageous.

title: Controller

title: CMC Regulatory Compliance Specialist
description:
Founded in 1969, Pharmathen has grown into a leading developer and manufacturer of specialized pharmaceutical products and one of the largest vertically integrated companies in advanced drug delivery technologies. With a strong international presence, we remain committed to improving people’s lives through innovation and access to affordable, high-quality medicines. Today, our products reach patients in more than 90 countries worldwide, supporting better health outcomes every day.

Pharmathen employs more than 1,600 people from over 27 different nationalities, reflecting a diverse and international workforce. Our achievements are driven by strong scientific expertise, high ethical standards, and the dedication of our people, who share a commitment to improving patient lives.

Pharmathen offers a great opportunity for career development and is seeking to recruit a CMC Regulatory Compliance Specialist to join our R&D team at our Metamorfosi premises.

As a CMC Regulatory Compliance Specialist, the ideal candidate will be responsible for supporting all pre- and post- approval CMC activities and acts as a liaison person with all relevant departments within Pharmathen as well as suppliers.

Requirements

What you will do:

More particularly:

  • Keeps abreast of international legislation, regulatory guidelines, and customer requirements.
  • Collects and collates a wide range of product technical information and ensures compliance with all applicable quality and regulatory guidelines.
  • Supports all pre-approval CMC activities by compiling product dossiers, including preparing and reviewing Modules 2 and 3, compiling Modules 4 and 5, and responding to Deficiency Letters (DLs) within established timelines.
  • Supports post-approval CMC activities by preparing quality variation packages and renewals for DCPs, MRPs, CPs, and national applications, and by responding to relevant Deficiency Letters (DLs) within strict deadlines.
  • Participates in teleconferences and meetings with regulatory authorities, suppliers, clients, and internal stakeholders across the organization.
  • Actively participates, where relevant, in new product development and lifecycle management activities, including registered product variation strategy assessments, to ensure ongoing regulatory compliance.

The ideal candidate should have:

  • Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in a scientific discipline (preferably Chemical Sciences, or Biochemistry)
  • 5-7 years relevant experience in the pharmaceutical area
  • Experience in analytical chemistry (e.g. HPLC) is considered an asset

Job-Specific Skills:

  • Excellent communication in English language (writing & speaking)
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines
  • Computer literacy
  • Project management
  • Multi-tasking
  • Time management

Benefits

What you'll gain:

  • Involvement in a high-caliber, team-oriented and dynamic atmosphere
  • Exposure to challenging business issues and practices
  • Great opportunity to leverage and develop your business knowledge and skills

Join our team and experience the unique Pharmathen’s culture that gives you the opportunity to innovate, to make decisions, to achieve your own potential and to chart your own career.

Pharmathen is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications regardless of gender, race, age, religion, sexual orientation, and national origin.

title: Quality Technician I - Nights
description:

title: 3rd & 1st Shift Direct Care
description:

title: Controller/Director of Finance
description:
A growing, privately held professional services organization is seeking an experienced, hands-on Controller / Director of Finance to manage financial operations, reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and revenue management across the business.


The organization operates across multiple business lines, including employee benefits, retirement and wealth management, payroll, and human resources. This role will help bring those areas together financially, giving the CFO, COO, and leadership team a clear and accurate view of revenue, expenses, profitability, cash flow, sales performance, and future growth.


This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys both the details and the bigger picture. The right candidate will be comfortable reconciling accounts and commissions, managing billing and receivables, developing budgets and forecasts, analyzing profitability, and turning financial data into practical business insights. This position will report to and work closely with the CFO and COO.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management & Reporting

  • Manage day-to-day financial operations and accounting processes.
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting.
  • Develop profit and loss reporting by business segment, including Benefits, Retirement and Wealth Management, Payroll, and HR.
  • Develop client-level and business-line profitability reporting.
  • Reconcile operating and other company bank accounts and maintain appropriate financial controls.
  • Manage accounts payable, cash flow, and company financial obligations.

Billing & Accounts Receivable

  • Oversee client billing across all service lines.
  • Ensure recurring billing and subscriptions are established and maintained accurately.
  • Monitor accounts receivable and follow up on outstanding client balances.
  • Reconcile contracted client services against actual billing to identify missed or incorrect revenue.

Commissions & Revenue Reconciliation

  • Manage commission reconciliation across insurance brokerage, broker-dealer, and investment advisory operations.
  • Track expected commissions against amounts received and research discrepancies.
  • Coordinate commission allocations and representative/producer payouts as applicable.
  • Develop reporting by client, producer, carrier, product, and business line.

Sales Tracking & Forecasting

  • Partner with leadership and sales teams to ensure new sales are properly recorded and tracked.
  • Reconcile closed sales against revenue and commissions received.
  • Maintain sales pipeline and revenue forecasting.
  • Develop reporting that connects the full revenue cycle from pipeline and closed sale through billing, cash received, and profitability.

Budgeting & Financial Planning

  • Support the senior leadership team in the annual budgeting process.
  • Develop budgets and forecasts by business segment.
  • Maintain rolling revenue, expense, and cash flow forecasts.
  • Analyze actual results against budget and identify trends, risks, and opportunities.
  • Assist leadership with financial modeling for staffing, pricing, new services, technology investments, and other strategic initiatives.

Payroll Financial Operations

  • Reconcile payroll-related bank accounts, including payroll tax funding and tax disbursements.
  • Reconcile client tax liabilities and other payroll-related pass-through funds.
  • Maintain appropriate controls and separation between client payroll funds and company operating funds.
  • Work with Payroll Operations to research and resolve financial discrepancies.
